scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9058: I'm on PC0 (20.1.1.x) and I can no longer get through
to PC12 (120.1.1.x) on the far side of the network -- it times out every
single time. This used to work, so something has broken on your side. I have
heard our two sides run on "different routing"; I won't pretend to know what
that means, but whatever connects the two sides is yours to run and it is
clearly not doing its job. Take a look and fix it today, please.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF core is converged, R11 redistributes
  between OSPF and EIGRP, and PC0 (20.1.1.x) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss
  in both directions. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a redistribution / interior-link fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12
across the OSPF/EIGRP core -- is NOT reproducible: the OSPF backbone is converged,
R11 redistributes OSPF<->EIGRP (so the 120.x/EIGRP prefixes appear in the OSPF
RIB and vice versa), and PC0 reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-core reachability is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
path, finds it working, optionally confirms R11's redistribution and the EIGRP
neighbors are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a broken
redistribution or a down interior link to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A thorough five-phase investigation found no active or historical fault that explains the reported PC0→PC12 timeout.

**Affected component / Topology context:** The path from PC0 (20.1.1.x) to PC12 (120.1.1.x) spans two routing domains: an OSPF backbone (r1 through r9, areas 0.0.0.0–0.0.0.4) and an EIGRP island (r12, r13, managed by EIGRP AS 100). r11 is the boundary router that runs both protocols simultaneously and redistributes EIGRP routes into OSPF, making PC12's prefix (120.0.0.0/8) reachable to the OSPF side.

**Mechanism check:** The redistribution chain was verified end-to-end. r11 holds a live EIGRP route `120.0.0.0/8 via 112.1.1.2 eth0` (r12); r1 holds `120.0.0.0/8 via 111.1.1.2 proto ospf` (r11); and r12 carries a stable kernel default route to 112.1.1.1 (r11). Live ping at test time showed 0% loss in both directions.

**OSPF flags from helper — all dismissed:** r12 and r13 have no OSPF configuration because they run EIGRP only — expected. r8's "orphaned area 0.0.0.2" flag is a false positive: area 2 is a stub (the BB segment plus loopbacks), r8 is its sole ABR, and the r4↔r8 virtual link through area 1 (confirmed by matching `area 1 virtual-link` statements on both ends with active adjacencies) connects it to the backbone. r8's loopbacks (18.x.x.x) appear correctly in other routers' tables.

**Root cause:** No fault found. The user-reported timeout is unconfirmed — no flap process, no carrier changes, no daemon errors, and no mis-redistribution is present. The claim is consistent with a transient routing-convergence delay during lab startup, which had resolved by the time of this investigation.

**Fix:** No corrective action required; current state is fully healthy.
